title: Intermittent open on a single I/O, appearing only in the cold half of temperature cycling, on a wire-bond PBGA

device.package: PBGA 256, wire bond, Cu wire on Al pad

samples.condition_as_received: still soldered to the customer's TC coupon board
sibling from the same assembly lot, never cycled
second failing unit from the same TC coupon lot

complaint: During board-level temperature cycling (-40 to +125 C) on a qualification coupon, 3 of 40 assemblies showed intermittent loss of continuity on one I/O net. The failure appears somewhere below about -10 C and clears on warm-up. The units pass every test at room temperature. The customer's CM has looked at the solder joints and believes it is a solder-joint crack; they want us to confirm so they can change the reflow profile.

symptoms.failure_rate: 3 of 40 assemblies on the TC coupon; failures began appearing after roughly 400 cycles. Zero failures at incoming electrical test and zero at room temperature at any point.
symptoms.conditions: Board-level TC -40 to +125 C, 2 cycles/hour. Failure is a continuity open on one I/O net, present only in the cold portion of the cycle, and it recovers completely on warm-up. Not reproducible at room temperature by any means the customer tried.

life_history.board_reflow: standard Pb-free reflow, MSL 3 handling documented and within floor life
life_history.application_notes: board-level qual coupon, daisy-chained continuity monitoring available on the customer's fixture

observations.conditions: 5 insertions at room temperature, customer program rev
observations.result: Passes all 5 insertions at room temperature. No parameter outside limits.
observations.interpretation: Room-temperature testing cannot see this failure; the case cannot proceed on room-temperature evidence.

open_questions: Does the open follow the package or the board? The customer has not yet re-tested the same package on a different board, or a different package on the same board site.
Which specific net and which specific ball/wire - the customer reports 'one I/O net' but has not identified it by ball position.
Is the assembly lot common across the three failures, and is it common with the 37 passing assemblies?
Cu wire on Al pad with an automotive mission profile - what does the OSAT's bond monitoring data for AS-26-0119 look like?
